claim: Macrophages destroy pathogens and diseased cells through Fcγ receptor (FcγR)-driven phagocytosis of antibody-opsonized targets.
source: Macrophages destroy pathogens and diseased cells through Fcγ receptor (FcγR)-driven phagocytosis of antibody-opsonized targets.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about macrophage function.

claim: Phagocytosis requires activation of multiple FcγRs.
source: Phagocytosis requires activation of multiple FcγRs, but the mechanism controlling the threshold for response is unclear.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, though the mechanism is unclear.

claim: Reducing ligand spacing from 17.5 nm to 7 nm potently enhances engulfment when the number of ligands remains constant.
source: When the number of ligands remains constant, reducing ligand spacing from 17.5 nm to 7 nm potently enhances engulfment, primarily by increasing efficiency of the engulfment-initiation process.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Tighter ligand clustering increases receptor phosphorylation.
source: Tighter ligand clustering increases receptor phosphorylation, as well as proximal downstream signals.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Tighter ligand clustering increases proximal downstream signals.
source: Tighter ligand clustering increases receptor phosphorylation, as well as proximal downstream signals.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Increasing the number of signaling domains recruited to a single ligand-receptor complex was not sufficient to recapitulate the effect of tight ligand clustering.
source: Increasing the number of signaling domains recruited to a single ligand-receptor complex was not sufficient to recapitulate this effect, indicating that clustering of multiple receptors is required.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Clustering of multiple receptors is required for enhanced engulfment.
source: Increasing the number of signaling domains recruited to a single ligand-receptor complex was not sufficient to recapitulate this effect, indicating that clustering of multiple receptors is required.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results showing that tandem signaling domains are insufficient.

claim: Macrophages use information about local ligand densities to make critical engulfment decisions.
source: Our results suggest that macrophages use information about local ligand densities to make critical engulfment decisions, which has implications for the mechanism of antibody-mediated phagocytosis and the design of immunotherapies.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and represents an interpretation of the findings.

claim: ADCP is a key mechanism of action for rituximab.
source: ADCP is a key mechanism of action for several cancer immunotherapies including rituximab, trastuzumab, and cetuximab (Chao et al., 2010; Uchida et al., 2004; Watanabe et al., 1999; Weiskopf et al., 2013; Weiskopf and Weissman, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: ADCP is a key mechanism of action for trastuzumab.
source: ADCP is a key mechanism of action for several cancer immunotherapies including rituximab, trastuzumab, and cetuximab (Chao et al., 2010; Uchida et al., 2004; Watanabe et al., 1999; Weiskopf et al., 2013; Weiskopf and Weissman, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: ADCP is a key mechanism of action for cetuximab.
source: ADCP is a key mechanism of action for several cancer immunotherapies including rituximab, trastuzumab, and cetuximab (Chao et al., 2010; Uchida et al., 2004; Watanabe et al., 1999; Weiskopf et al., 2013; Weiskopf and Weissman, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Activation of multiple FcγRs is required for a macrophage to engulf a three-dimensional target.
source: Activation of multiple FcγRs is required for a macrophage to engulf a three-dimensional target.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: FcγR-IgG must be present across the entire target to drive progressive closure of the phagocytic cup that surrounds the target.
source: FcγR-IgG must be present across the entire target to drive progressive closure of the phagocytic cup that surrounds the target (Griffin et al., 1975).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: A critical antibody threshold across an entire target dictates an all-or-none engulfment response by the macrophage.
source: In addition, a critical antibody threshold across an entire target dictates an all-or-none engulfment response by the macrophage (Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Receptor clustering plays a role in regulating digital responses in other immune cells.
source: Although the mechanism of this thresholded response remains unclear, receptor clustering plays a role in regulating digital responses in other immune cells (Berger et al., 2020; Davis and van der Merwe, 2006; Holowka and Baird, 1996; Kato et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2020; Veneziano et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: FcγR clustering may regulate phagocytosis.
source: FcγR clustering may also regulate phagocytosis (Goodridge et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: IgG-bound FcγRs form clusters within the plasma membrane.
source: High-resolution imaging of macrophages has demonstrated that IgG-bound FcγRs form clusters (resolution of >100 nm) within the plasma membrane (Lin et al., 2016; Lopes et al., 2017; Sobota et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: FcγR clusters recruit downstream effector proteins such as Syk-kinase and phosphoinositide 3-kinase.
source: These small clusters, which recruit downstream effector proteins such as Syk-kinase and phosphoinositide 3-kinase, eventually coalesce into larger micron-scale patches as they migrate towards the center of the cell-target synapse (Jaumouillé et al., 2014; Lin et al., 2016; Lopes et al., 2017; Sobota et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: FcγR clusters eventually coalesce into larger micron-scale patches as they migrate towards the center of the cell-target synapse.
source: These small clusters, which recruit downstream effector proteins such as Syk-kinase and phosphoinositide 3-kinase, eventually coalesce into larger micron-scale patches as they migrate towards the center of the cell-target synapse (Jaumouillé et al., 2014; Lin et al., 2016; Lopes et al., 2017; Sobota et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The DNA-CARγ can drive specific engulfment of DNA-bound beads in both RAW264.7 and THP-1 cells.
source: The DNA-CARγ drove specific engulfment of DNA-bound beads in both RAW264.7 and THP-1 cells (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The extent of engulfment mediated by DNA-CARγ was similar to IgG-coated beads.
source: The extent of engulfment was similar to IgG-coated beads, and the ligand density required for robust phagocytosis was also comparable to IgG [Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Bakalar et al., 2018; Morrissey et al., 2020].
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data and comparison to prior literature.

claim: Cells expressing the DNA-CARadhesion failed to induce engulfment of DNA-functionalized beads.
source: As a control, we tested a variant of the DNA-CAR that lacked the intracellular domain of the FcRγ chain (DNA-CARadhesion). Cells expressing the DNA-CARadhesion failed to induce engulfment of DNA-functionalized beads (Figure 1C), demonstrating that this process depends upon the signaling domain of the FcγR.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Engulfment of DNA-functionalized beads depends upon the signaling domain of the FcγR.
source: Cells expressing the DNA-CARadhesion failed to induce engulfment of DNA-functionalized beads (Figure 1C), demonstrating that this process depends upon the signaling domain of the FcγR.
evidence: This is inferred from the control experiment showing lack of engulfment without the signaling domain.

claim: The average fluorescence intensity of recruited DNA-CARγ receptor correlated with the number of ligands presented by individual origami pegboards.
source: Using signal from the 72 ligand (72L) origami pegboard as an internal intensity standard of brightness, and thus correcting for differences in illumination between wells, we found that the average fluorescence intensity correlated with the number of ligands presented by individual origami pegboards (Figure 2D, E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Syk intensity increased as a function of the number of ligands present on each origami pegboard.
source: In addition, we measured Syk recruitment to individual DNA origami pegboards and found that Syk intensity also increased as a function of the number of ligands present on each origami pegboard (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Increasing the number of ligands per cluster increased engulfment, but engulfment plateaued at a cluster size of eight ligands.
source: We found that increasing the number of ligands per cluster increased engulfment, but that engulfment plateaued at a cluster size of eight ligands (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The observed engulfment phenotype was ligand, receptor, and FcγR signaling dependent.
source: We confirmed that the observed engulfment phenotype was both ligand, receptor, and FcγR signaling dependent (Figure 3C, D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: FcγR clustering strongly enhances engulfment up to a cluster size of eight ligands.
source: Together, these data reveal that FcγR clustering strongly enhances engulfment up to a cluster size of eight ligands.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The efficiency of macrophage engulfment was approximately twofold higher for the 4T-functionalized beads when compared to the 4M or 4S beads.
source: We found that the efficiency of macrophage engulfment was approximately twofold higher for the 4T-functionalized beads when compared to the 4M or 4S beads (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Human THP-1 cells expressing the DNA-CARγ showed the same ligand spacing dependence as RAW264.7 cells.
source: Human THP-1 cells expressing the DNA-CARγ showed the same ligand spacing dependence (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The efficiency of macrophage engulfment was dependent on ligand spacing for all DNA-CAR constructs tested.
source: We found that the efficiency of macrophage engulfment was dependent on ligand spacing for all constructs tested (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Engulfment of beads functionalized with both the 4T and the 4S origami platforms was dependent on the FcγR signaling domain.
source: Expression of the various DNA-CARs at the cell cortex was comparable, and engulfment of beads functionalized with both the 4T and the 4S origami platforms was dependent on the FcγR signaling domain (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Macrophages preferentially engulf targets with tighter ligand clusters.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that macrophages preferentially engulf targets with tighter ligand clusters.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: There was no difference in DNA-CARγ-BFP recruitment to 4T and 4S beads.
source: However, when we measured the total fluorescence intensity of receptors at the phagocytic cup, we did not detect a difference in DNA-CARγ-BFP recruitment to 4T and 4S beads (Figure 6A, B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: 4T origami beads were preferentially engulfed over 4M or 4S origami beads when using 16mer high-affinity ligands.
source: Using these 16mer high-affinity ligands, we found that 4T origami beads were still preferentially engulfed over 4M or 4S origami beads (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: An avidity effect is not the cause of the preferential engulfment of targets having tightly spaced ligands.
source: These results suggest that an avidity effect is not the cause of the preferential engulfment of targets having tightly spaced ligands.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data using high-affinity ligands.

claim: Macrophages interacted with beads functionalized with the 4T and 4S pegboards with comparable frequency.
source: Macrophages interacted with beads functionalized with the 4T and 4S pegboards with comparable frequency (46 ± 7% total bead-cell contacts vs. 54 ± 7% total bead-cell contacts, respectively).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: The probability of engulfment initiation was significantly higher for the 4T (95 ± 5% of bead contacts) versus 4S (61 ± 9% of bead contacts) beads.
source: However, the probability of engulfment initiation was significantly higher for the 4T (95 ± 5% of bead contacts) versus 4S (61 ± 9% of bead contacts) beads, and the probability that initiation events resulted in successful completion of engulfment was higher for 4T (69 ± 9% of initiation events) versus 4S (39 ± 11% of initiation events) beads (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The probability that initiation events resulted in successful completion of engulfment was higher for 4T (69 ± 9% of initiation events) versus 4S (39 ± 11% of initiation events) beads.
source: However, the probability of engulfment initiation was significantly higher for the 4T (95 ± 5% of bead contacts) versus 4S (61 ± 9% of bead contacts) beads, and the probability that initiation events resulted in successful completion of engulfment was higher for 4T (69 ± 9% of initiation events) versus 4S (39 ± 11% of initiation events) beads (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The time from contact to engulfment initiation was ~300 s longer for beads functionalized with 4S origami pegboards than beads containing 4T origami pegboards.
source: In addition, for beads that were engulfed, the time from contact to engulfment initiation was ~300 s longer for beads functionalized with 4S origami pegboards than beads containing 4T origami pegboards (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Once initiated, the time from initiation to completion of engulfment did not differ significantly for beads coated with 4T or 4S origami.
source: However, once initiated, the time from initiation to completion of engulfment did not differ significantly for beads coated with 4T or 4S origami (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: 66 ± 8% of 4T bead contacts resulted in successful engulfment compared to 24 ± 8% for 4S beads.
source: Overall, 66 ± 8% of 4T bead contacts resulted in successful engulfment compared to 24 ± 8% for 4S beads (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: DNA-CARadhesion macrophages rarely met the initiation criteria.
source: The DNA-CARadhesion macrophages rarely met the initiation criteria, suggesting that active signaling from the FcγR is required (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Active signaling from the FcγR is required for engulfment initiation.
source: The DNA-CARadhesion macrophages rarely met the initiation criteria, suggesting that active signaling from the FcγR is required (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the control experiment with DNA-CARadhesion.

claim: Tighter spacing between ligands within a cluster enhances the probability and kinetics of initiating engulfment.
source: Together, these data reveal that tighter spacing between ligands within a cluster enhances the probability and kinetics of initiating engulfment, as well as the overall success frequency of completing engulfment, but does not affect the rate of phagosome closure once initiated.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Tighter spacing between ligands within a cluster enhances the overall success frequency of completing engulfment.
source: Together, these data reveal that tighter spacing between ligands within a cluster enhances the probability and kinetics of initiating engulfment, as well as the overall success frequency of completing engulfment, but does not affect the rate of phagosome closure once initiated.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Tighter spacing between ligands within a cluster does not affect the rate of phagosome closure once initiated.
source: Together, these data reveal that tighter spacing between ligands within a cluster enhances the probability and kinetics of initiating engulfment, as well as the overall success frequency of completing engulfment, but does not affect the rate of phagosome closure once initiated.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: 4T phagocytic cups recruited more tSH2-Syk than the 4S beads.
source: We found that 4T phagocytic cups recruited more tSH2-Syk than the 4S beads, indicating an increase in receptor phosphorylation by nanoclustered ligands.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Nanoclustered ligands increase receptor phosphorylation.
source: We found that 4T phagocytic cups recruited more tSH2-Syk than the 4S beads, indicating an increase in receptor phosphorylation by nanoclustered ligands.
evidence: This is inferred from the increased tSH2-Syk recruitment.

claim: Generation of PIP3 at the phagocytic cup increased at 4T relative to 4S synapses.
source: Generation of PIP3 and actin filaments at the phagocytic cup also increased at 4T relative to 4S synapses (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Generation of actin filaments at the phagocytic cup increased at 4T relative to 4S synapses.
source: Generation of PIP3 and actin filaments at the phagocytic cup also increased at 4T relative to 4S synapses (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Differential recruitment of downstream signaling molecules to 4T versus 4S origami beads was most apparent in early and mid-stage phagocytic cups.
source: This differential recruitment of downstream signaling molecules to 4T versus 4S origami beads was most apparent in early and mid-stage phagocytic cups; late-stage cups showed only a slightly significant difference in tSH2-Syk recruitment and no significant differences in generation of PIP3 or actin filaments (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Nanoscale ligand spacing affects early downstream signaling events involved in phagocytic cup formation.
source: Together, these data demonstrate that nanoscale ligand spacing affects early downstream signaling events involved in phagocytic cup formation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: DNA-CAR-4xγ macrophages failed to engulf the high-affinity 1-ligand origami beads.
source: While the DNA-CAR-1xγ−3xΔITAM-expressing macrophages engulfed 4T origami beads, the DNA-CAR-4xγ macrophages failed to engulf the high-affinity 1-ligand origami beads (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: DNA-CAR-1xγ−3xΔITAM-expressing macrophages engulfed 4T origami beads.
source: While the DNA-CAR-1xγ−3xΔITAM-expressing macrophages engulfed 4T origami beads, the DNA-CAR-4xγ macrophages failed to engulf the high-affinity 1-ligand origami beads (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: The tight clustering of multiple receptors is necessary for engulfment.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that the tight clustering of multiple receptors is necessary for engulfment and increasing the number of intracellular signaling modules on a single receptor is not sufficient to surpass the threshold for activation of engulfment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Increasing the number of intracellular signaling modules on a single receptor is not sufficient to surpass the threshold for activation of engulfment.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that the tight clustering of multiple receptors is necessary for engulfment and increasing the number of intracellular signaling modules on a single receptor is not sufficient to surpass the threshold for activation of engulfment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Tight ligand clustering increases the probability of initiating phagocytosis by enhancing FcγR phosphorylation.
source: We found that tight ligand clustering increases the probability of initiating phagocytosis by enhancing FcγR phosphorylation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Phagocytosis requires IgG across the entire target surface to initiate local receptor activation and to 'zipper' close the phagocytic cup.
source: Phagocytosis requires IgG across the entire target surface to initiate local receptor activation and to 'zipper' close the phagocytic cup (Freeman et al., 2016; Griffin et al., 1975).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Incomplete opsonization of a target surface, or micron-scale spaces between IgG patches, decreases engulfment.
source: Consistent with this zipper model, incomplete opsonization of a target surface, or micron-scale spaces between IgG patches, decreases engulfment (Freeman et al., 2016; Griffin et al., 1975).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A critical IgG threshold is needed to activate the final stages of phagocytosis.
source: While this model has largely fallen out of favor, more recent studies have found that a critical IgG threshold is needed to activate the final stages of phagocytosis (Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: There may be a nanoscale density-dependent trigger for receptor phosphorylation and downstream signaling.
source: Our data suggest that there may also be a nanoscale density-dependent trigger for receptor phosphorylation and downstream signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Both tight nanoscale IgG-FcγR clustering and a uniform distribution of IgG across the target are needed to direct signaling to 'zipper' close the phagocytic cup.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that both tight nanoscale IgG-FcγR clustering and a uniform distribution of IgG across the target are needed to direct signaling to 'zipper' close the phagocytic cup.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and integration with prior knowledge.

claim: Macrophages constantly encounter background 'eat me' signals.
source: Macrophages constantly encounter background 'eat me' signals (Gonzalez-Quintela et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Hyper-local density measurement may buffer macrophages against background stimuli and weakly opsonized targets.
source: This hyper-local density measurement may buffer macrophages against background stimuli and weakly opsonized targets that are unlikely to have adjacent bound antibodies, while still robustly detecting and efficiently engulfing highly opsonized targets.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: FcγR crosslinking correlates with increased ITAM phosphorylation.
source: Our findings are consistent with previous results demonstrating that FcγR crosslinking correlates with increased ITAM phosphorylation (Huang et al., 1992; Kwiatkowska and Sobota, 2001; Lin et al., 2016; Sobota et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Nanoscale ligand clustering does not noticeably affect the amount of ligand-bound receptor at the phagocytic cup.
source: Specifically, we demonstrate that nanoscale ligand clustering does not noticeably affect the amount of ligand-bound receptor at the phagocytic cup, and that ligand spacing continues to affect engulfment when avidity effects are diminished through the use of high-affinity receptor-ligands.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Ligand spacing continues to affect engulfment when avidity effects are diminished through the use of high-affinity receptor-ligands.
source: Specifically, we demonstrate that nanoscale ligand clustering does not noticeably affect the amount of ligand-bound receptor at the phagocytic cup, and that ligand spacing continues to affect engulfment when avidity effects are diminished through the use of high-affinity receptor-ligands.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Changes in receptor binding or recruitment caused by increased avidity are unlikely to account for the increased potency of clustered ligands.
source: Collectively, these data reveal that changes in receptor binding or recruitment caused by increased avidity are unlikely to account for the increased potency of clustered ligands.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Receptor clustering does not simply increase the local intracellular concentration of FcγR signaling domains.
source: Our data also exclude the possibility that receptor clustering simply increases the local intracellular concentration of FcγR signaling domains as arranging FcγR ITAMs in tandem did not have the same effect as clustering multiple receptor-ligand interactions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Segregated liquid-ordered and liquid-disordered membrane domains around immune receptor clusters have been reported to promote receptor phosphorylation.
source: Segregated liquid-ordered and liquid-disordered membrane domains around immune receptor clusters have been reported to promote receptor phosphorylation (Bag et al., 2020; Dinic et al., 2015; Eggeling et al., 2009; Kabouridis, 2006; Simons and Ikonen, 1997; Sohn et al., 2006; Stone et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: FcγR clusters are associated with liquid-ordered domains.
source: FcγR clusters are associated with liquid-ordered domains (Beekman et al., 2008; Katsumata et al., 2001; Kwiatkowska and Sobota, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Liquid-ordered domains recruit Src family kinases, which phosphorylate FcγRs.
source: Liquid-ordered domains recruit Src family kinases, which phosphorylate FcγRs, while liquid-disordered domains are enriched in the transmembrane phosphatase CD45, which dephosphorylates FcγRs (Bag et al., 2020; Sohn et al., 2006; Stone et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Liquid-disordered domains are enriched in the transmembrane phosphatase CD45, which dephosphorylates FcγRs.
source: Liquid-ordered domains recruit Src family kinases, which phosphorylate FcγRs, while liquid-disordered domains are enriched in the transmembrane phosphatase CD45, which dephosphorylates FcγRs (Bag et al., 2020; Sohn et al., 2006; Stone et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Lipid ordering could provide a mechanism that leads to receptor activation if denser receptor-ligand clusters are more efficient in nucleating or associating with ordered lipid domains.
source: Thus, lipid ordering could provide a mechanism that leads to receptor activation if denser receptor-ligand clusters are more efficient in nucleating or associating with ordered lipid domains.
evidence: This is a speculative model proposed to explain the findings.

claim: CD45 is heavily glycosylated, making the extracellular domain 25–40 nm tall.
source: CD45 is heavily glycosylated, making the extracellular domain 25–40 nm tall (Davis and van der Merwe, 2006; McCall et al., 1992; Woollett et al., 1985).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: CD45 is excluded from close cell-cell contacts, such as those mediated by IgG-FcγR, which have a dimension of 11.5 nm.
source: Because of its size, CD45 is excluded from close cell-cell contacts, such as those mediated by IgG-FcγR, which have a dimension of 11.5 nm (Bakalar et al., 2018; Burroughs et al., 2011; Carbone et al., 2017; Chung et al., 2013; Lu et al., 2011; Schmid et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: IgG bound to antigens ≤ 10.5 nm from the target surface induces CD45 exclusion and engulfment.
source: IgG bound to antigens ≤ 10.5 nm from the target surface induces CD45 exclusion and engulfment (estimated total intermembrane distance of ≤22 nm Bakalar et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: A higher receptor-ligand density constrains membrane shape fluctuations.
source: A higher receptor-ligand density constrains membrane shape fluctuations (Krobath et al., 2009; Krobath et al., 2011; Różycki et al., 2010), and this constraint may increase CD45 exclusion (Schmid et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature and represents a speculative mechanism.

claim: DNA-CARs are single-chain receptors that recruit one intracellular signaling domain per ligand, similar to the single-chain human FcγRIIA receptor.
source: Our DNA-CARs are single-chain receptors that recruit one intracellular signaling domain per ligand, similar to the single-chain human FcγRIIA receptor (Nimmerjahn and Ravetch, 2006).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental system with comparison to endogenous receptors.

claim: High-affinity FcRIIA alleles correlate with an increase in effectiveness of the ADCP-inducing drug rituximab.
source: FcγRIIA is ubiquitously expressed on human myeloid cells, and high-affinity FcRIIA alleles correlate with an increase in effectiveness of the ADCP-inducing drug rituximab and lupus susceptibility (Bruhns and Jönsson, 2015; Nimmerjahn and Ravetch, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: High-affinity FcRIIA alleles correlate with lupus susceptibility.
source: FcγRIIA is ubiquitously expressed on human myeloid cells, and high-affinity FcRIIA alleles correlate with an increase in effectiveness of the ADCP-inducing drug rituximab and lupus susceptibility (Bruhns and Jönsson, 2015; Nimmerjahn and Ravetch, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The majority of FcγR family members are multimeric complexes composed of a ligand-binding α chain and a dimerized signaling γ chain.
source: The majority of FcγR family members, including all activating mouse FcγRs and the human FcγRI and FcγRIIIA, are multimeric complexes composed of a ligand-binding α chain and a dimerized signaling γ chain.
evidence: This is established knowledge about FcγR structure.

claim: Ligand spacing had a similar effect on phagocytosis when the CD86 transmembrane domain was replaced with the Fcα or Fcγ transmembrane domain.
source: We found that ligand spacing had a similar effect on phagocytosis when we replaced the CD86 transmembrane domain with the Fcα or Fcγ transmembrane domain.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: The Fcγ transmembrane domain construct triggered more bead internalization across all conditions compared to the CD86 transmembrane domain.
source: However, the Fcγ transmembrane domain construct triggered more bead internalization across all conditions.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: Engineered multivalent Fc oligomers revealed that IgE ligand geometry alters Fcε receptor signaling in mast cells.
source: Engineered multivalent Fc oligomers revealed that IgE ligand geometry alters Fcε receptor signaling in mast cells (Sil et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Some systems, like integrin-mediated cell adhesion, appear to have very discrete threshold requirements for ligand spacing.
source: Some systems, like integrin-mediated cell adhesion, appear to have very discrete threshold requirements for ligand spacing while others, like T cell activation, appear to continuously improve with reduced intermolecular spacing (Arnold et al., 2004; Cai et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: T cell activation appears to continuously improve with reduced intermolecular spacing.
source: Some systems, like integrin-mediated cell adhesion, appear to have very discrete threshold requirements for ligand spacing while others, like T cell activation, appear to continuously improve with reduced intermolecular spacing (Arnold et al., 2004; Cai et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: As the intermembrane distance between T cell and target increases, the requirement for tight ligand spacing becomes more stringent.
source: Interestingly, as the intermembrane distance between T cell and target increases, the requirement for tight ligand spacing becomes more stringent (Cai et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: IgG bound to tall antigens may be more dependent on tight nanocluster spacing than short antigens.
source: This suggests that IgG bound to tall antigens may be more dependent on tight nanocluster spacing than short antigens.
evidence: This is a speculative inference drawn from prior literature findings.

claim: Antibody therapies that rely on FcγR engagement are used to treat cancer, autoimmune, and neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Antibody therapies that rely on FcγR engagement are used to treat cancer, autoimmune, and neurodegenerative diseases (Chao et al., 2010; Nimmerjahn and Ravetch, 2005; Uchida et al., 2004; Watanabe et al., 1999; Weiskopf et al., 2013; Weiskopf and Weissman, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Multimerizing Fc domains or targeting multiple antibodies to the same antigen may increase antibody potency.
source: Multimerizing Fc domains or targeting multiple antibodies to the same antigen may increase antibody potency (Zhang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature and represents a speculative application.

claim: Rituximab has two binding sites on its target antigen.
source: Interestingly, rituximab, a successful anti-CD20 therapy that potently induces ADCP, has two binding sites on its target antigen (Zhao et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Selecting clustered antigens or pharmacologically inducing antigen clustering may increase antibody potency.
source: Selecting clustered antigens or pharmacologically inducing antigen clustering may also increase antibody potency (Chew et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature and represents a speculative application.

claim: Antibody engineering strategies that optimize spacing of multiple antibodies could lead to stronger FcγR activation and potentially more effective therapies.
source: Our data suggest that antibody engineering strategies that optimize spacing of multiple antibodies through leucine zippers, cysteine bonds, DNA hybridization (Delcassian et al., 2013; Seifert et al., 2014; Sil et al., 2007), or multimeric scaffolds (Divine et al., 2020; Fallas et al., 2017; Huang et al., 2021; Ueda et al., 2020) could lead to stronger FcγR activation and potentially more effective therapies.
evidence: This is a speculative application of the findings with support from prior literature.
